blocks.text: The lymphatic system is an important and integral part of the body's vascular system; it is a complementary system alongside the venous system with which it develops intimately, possessing similar morphological features. The lymphatic vessels and the initial blood vessels are intimately intertwined within the interstitium which is a place of exchange and diffusion.

They arise from the lymphatic capillary networks of an organ or region. The number of lymphatic capillaries that come together to form lymphatic vessels varies greatly. The lymphatic vessels anastomose with each other and constitute the plexuses.

The lymphatic vessels exit the organ they drain, at the level of the entrance to the blood vessels. Leaving the organ, the lymphatic vessels come together and converge towards the regional lymph nodes; these are afferent vessels. After crossing the node(s), the lymphatic vessels (efferent vessels) head towards the large lymphatic collecting trunks: the thoracic duct or the large lymphatic vein, the right and left jugular and subclavian trunks
It is the main lymphatic vessel, approximately 45 cm long and 2 to 5 mm in diameter, draining lymph and chyle from almost the entire body.

2- The large lymphatic vein It is located on the right side of the neck. It is placed at the anterolateral part of the base of the neck, between the internal jugular and right subclavian veins. It has a length of 1 to 2 centimeters. It is formed by the union of the right jugular and subclavian trunks. It flows into the right anglevenous and receives the right bronchomediastinal trunk.

THE LYMPHOID ORGANS THE SPLEEN: Lymphoid, hematopoietic organ, branched off the portal system. It is located deep in the left hypochondrium, in the left subphrenic compartment. It is therefore a thoracoabdominal organ which normally escapes palpation.

THE THYMUS: Organ located in the antero-superior part of the mediastinum, in the thymic compartment, it is a median organ of pyramidal shape, present to describe two lobes attached to each other. Well developed in children. It regresses in adulthood.

THE BONE MARROW: Provides an important function. There are two types of bone marrow, red marrow (also called myeloid tissuee) and yellow marrow. It contains two types of stem cells. Hematopoietic cells are the origin of white blood cells, red blood cells and platelets. Mesenchymal cells differentiate to form bone, cartilaginous and muscular structures THE TONSILLAS or tonsils: secondary lymphoid organs which play a role in the body's defense. Examples: Palatine, pharyngeal and lingual tonsils

The lymphatic system is an important and integral part of the body's vascular system; it is a complementary system alongside the venous system. The lymphatic network is present throughout the body except in the central nervous system and non-vascularized tissues.

The right lymphatic duct (great lymphatic vein) It is located on the right side of the neck, formed by the union of the right jugular and subclavian trunks, and drains at the right venous angle.

The thoracic duct This is the main lymphatic vessel. It originates in the abdomen from the cisterna chyli and ascends in the posterior mediastinum, ending at the left jugulo-subclavian venous junction.

blocks.text: The lymphatic system is involved in all vital functions (nutrition processes, metabolism, immune defense mechanisms). It plays a part in pathological processes, including the dissemination of infections and metastasis of malignant tumors. It is also the site of lymphatic pathology such as lymphedema. The lymphatic system is responsible for the absorption of water, crystalloids, lipid emulsions, and foreign particle suspensions that do not enter the blood capillaries.
